cards.front: On a number line, numbers get [ ___ ] moving right and [ ___ ] moving left.
cards.back: On a number line, numbers get bigger moving right and smaller moving left.

options.text: On a number line, numbers get bigger moving right and smaller moving left.
options.explanation: Values increase as you move right along a number line and decrease as you move left, so numbers become bigger to the right and smaller to the left.

options.text: On a number line, numbers get smaller moving right and bigger moving left.
options.explanation: This reverses the direction of increasing values. Numbers become bigger when moving right along a number line and smaller when moving left.

options.text: On a number line, numbers get bigger moving right and bigger moving left.
options.explanation: Although values increase when moving right, they do not also increase when moving left. Numbers become smaller as you move left along a number line.

options.text: On a number line, numbers get smaller moving right and smaller moving left.
options.explanation: Although values decrease when moving left, they do not also decrease when moving right. Numbers become bigger as you move right along a number line.

cards.front: Which is smaller: $-6$ or $-2$?

options.explanation: Negative numbers farther to the left on a number line are smaller. Since $-6$ lies to the left of $-2$, it is the smaller value.
This treats the number closer to zero as smaller. Among negative numbers, the value farther from zero is smaller, so $-6$ is smaller than $-2$.
Dropping the negative sign changes the value to a positive number. Both given values are negative, and $-6$ is smaller because it lies farther left.
Using the magnitude alone ignores the negative signs. On the number line, $-6$ lies to the left of $-2$, making $-6$ the smaller number.

cards.front:
Which temperature is lowest: $4^
\circ\text{C}$, $-2^\circ\text{C}$, $-7^\circ\text{C}$ or $1^\circ\text{C}$?

options.explanation: The lowest temperature is represented by the smallest number. Since $-7$ is farther below zero than $-2$, it is the lowest of the four temperatures.
This identifies a negative temperature but not the lowest one. Since $-7$ is less than $-2$, the lowest temperature is $-7^\circ\text{C}$.
A positive temperature is higher than every negative temperature listed. The smallest value is $-7$, so the lowest temperature is $-7^\circ\text{C}$.
This confuses the greatest numerical value with the lowest temperature. Of the listed values, $-7$ is smallest, so the lowest temperature is $-7^\circ\text{C}$.

cards.front: Adding a positive number moves [ ___ ]; subtracting a positive number moves [ ___ ].
cards.back: Adding a positive number moves right; subtracting a positive number moves left.

options.text: Adding a positive number moves right; subtracting a positive number moves left.
options.explanation: Adding a positive value increases a number, which means moving right on the number line. Subtracting a positive value decreases it, which means moving left.

options.text: Adding a positive number moves left; subtracting a positive number moves right.
options.explanation: This reverses both operations. Adding a positive number increases the value and moves right, while subtracting a positive number decreases the value and moves left.

options.text: Adding a positive number moves right; subtracting a positive number moves right.
options.explanation: Subtracting a positive number does not increase the value. Addition moves right, but subtraction of a positive number decreases the value and therefore moves left.

options.text: Adding a positive number moves left; subtracting a positive number moves left.
options.explanation: Adding a positive number does not decrease the value. It moves right on the number line, whereas subtracting a positive number moves left.

cards.front: Adding a negative number moves [ ___ ]; subtracting a negative number moves [ ___ ].
cards.back: Adding a negative number moves left; subtracting a negative number moves right.

options.text: Adding a negative number moves left; subtracting a negative number moves right.
options.explanation: Adding a negative decreases the value, so it moves left. Subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding a positive, so it moves right.

options.text: Adding a negative number moves right; subtracting a negative number moves left.
options.explanation: This ignores how the negative sign changes each operation. Adding a negative moves left, while subtracting a negative becomes addition and moves right.

options.text: Adding a negative number moves left; subtracting a negative number moves left.
options.explanation: Adding a negative does move left, but subtracting a negative has the opposite effect. It is equivalent to adding a positive, so it moves right.

options.text: Adding a negative number moves right; subtracting a negative number moves right.
options.explanation: Subtracting a negative moves right, but adding a negative does not. Adding a value below zero decreases the result, so it moves left.

cards.front: Work out $6 - 11$.

options.explanation: Starting at $6$ and subtracting $11$ means moving eleven places left on the number line. This passes zero and finishes at $-5$.
This finds the difference between $11$ and $6$ but loses the sign. Since more is subtracted than the starting value, the result is $-5$.
This effectively makes both numbers negative and adds their magnitudes. Starting from positive $6$ and moving $11$ left gives $-5$, not $-17$.
This adds $6$ and $11$ instead of subtracting. Subtracting $11$ from $6$ moves past zero by five places, giving $-5$.

cards.front: Work out $-4 + (-6)$.

options.explanation: Adding two negative numbers means adding their magnitudes and keeping the negative sign. Since $4+6=10$, the result is $-10$.
This subtracts the magnitudes instead of adding them. Both terms are negative, so their magnitudes add: $4+6=10$, giving $-10$.
The magnitudes have been added correctly, but the negative sign has been lost. Adding two negative numbers produces a negative result, so the answer is $-10$.
This both subtracts the magnitudes and gives the result the wrong sign. Adding two negatives combines their magnitudes, so $-4+(-6)=-10$.

cards.front: Subtracting a negative is the same as [ ___ ] the positive version.
cards.back: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding the positive version.

options.explanation: Subtracting a negative reverses the subtraction operation, making it equivalent to adding the corresponding positive number. For example, $5-(-2)=5+2$.
Keeping subtraction unchanged overlooks the double negative. Subtracting a negative changes to adding the positive version, as in $5-(-2)=5+2$.
The rule that two negative signs produce a positive does not turn subtraction into multiplication. Subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding its positive version.
Negative signs can affect division signs, but no division occurs here. Subtracting a negative changes the operation to adding the corresponding positive number.

cards.front: Work out $9 - (-4)$.

options.explanation: Subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding the corresponding positive, so $9 - (-4) = 9 + 4 = 13$.
This treats the two minus signs as a single subtraction sign. Subtracting a negative becomes addition, so $9 - (-4) = 9 + 4 = 13$.
This incorrectly gives the result a negative sign. The two minus signs combine to make addition, giving $9 + 4 = 13$.
This subtracts $4$ from $9$ and then incorrectly makes the result negative. Subtracting $-4$ means adding $4$, so the answer is $13$.

cards.front: In $9 - -4$, what does the second minus sign belong to?

options.explanation: The first minus sign indicates subtraction, while the second is attached to $4$ and shows that the number being subtracted is negative.
The second minus sign does not belong to $9$; it is directly attached to $4$, making the number being subtracted $-4$.
The first minus sign is the subtraction operation, not what the second sign belongs to. The second minus sign belongs to $-4$.
The second minus sign specifically identifies $4$ as negative rather than applying to the entire expression. It therefore belongs to $-4$.

cards.front: Choose two numbers from $-8$, $-3$, $3$, $8$ that add to $-11$.

options.explanation: Adding the two negative numbers combines their magnitudes: $-8 + (-3) = -(8 + 3) = -11$.
These numbers have different signs, so their magnitudes are subtracted: $-8 + 3 = -5$. The pair that totals $-11$ is $-8$ and $-3$.
These numbers total $5$ because $-3 + 8 = 5$. To obtain $-11$, both selected numbers must be negative: $-8$ and $-3$.
Adding two positive numbers gives $3 + 8 = 11$, not $-11$. Choosing their negative counterparts, $-8$ and $-3$, gives the required total.

cards.front: If two numbers add to a negative answer, the [ ___ ] number or numbers have the bigger effect.
cards.back: If two numbers add to a negative answer, the negative number or numbers have the bigger effect.

options.explanation: A negative total means the negative values outweigh the positive values. Therefore, the negative number or numbers have the greater overall effect on the sum.
Positive numbers cannot have the bigger effect if the resulting sum is negative. The negative number or numbers must outweigh the positives.
Zero has no effect when added, so it cannot determine that a sum is negative. The negative number or numbers must have the bigger effect.
Even numbers are not inherently more influential in addition; their signs and magnitudes matter. A negative total shows that the negative numbers have the bigger effect.

cards.front: For multiplication or division, what sign do same signs give?

options.explanation: Multiplying or dividing two numbers with matching signs always gives a positive result, whether both original numbers are positive or both are negative.
A negative result comes from different signs, not matching signs. Two positive signs or two negative signs give a positive result in multiplication and division.
Matching signs do not make a product or quotient zero unless one number itself is zero. The sign rule gives a positive result.

options.text: The sign of the larger number
options.explanation: The sizes of the numbers affect the magnitude, not the sign of the result. For multiplication or division, matching signs always give a positive sign.

cards.front: For multiplication or division, what sign do different signs give?

options.explanation: Multiplying or dividing numbers with different signs always gives a negative result: one positive sign and one negative sign produce a negative answer.
A positive result comes from matching signs, not different signs. One positive number and one negative number give a negative product or quotient.
Different signs do not make the result zero unless one of the numbers is zero. The multiplication and division sign rule gives a negative result.

options.text: The sign of the larger number
options.explanation: The larger number determines the magnitude but not the result’s sign. Different signs always produce a negative result in multiplication or division.

cards.front: Work out $-7 \times 5$.

options.explanation: The signs are different, so the product is negative. Since $7 \times 5 = 35$, it follows that $-7 \times 5 = -35$.
This has the correct magnitude but ignores the different-sign rule. A negative number multiplied by a positive number gives a negative result, so the answer is $-35$.
This comes from adding $-7$ and $5$ instead of multiplying them. The required calculation is $7 \times 5 = 35$, with a negative sign, giving $-35$.
This uses $6 \times 5$ rather than $7 \times 5$, an off-by-one multiplication error. The correct magnitude is $35$, and different signs make it $-35$.

cards.front: Work out $-42 \div (-6)$.

options.explanation: Both numbers are negative, so their quotient is positive. Since $42 \div 6 = 7$, the value of $-42 \div (-6)$ is $7$.
This keeps one negative sign instead of applying the same-sign rule. Dividing two negative numbers gives a positive result, so the answer is $7$.
This reverses the familiar fact that $6 \times 7 = 42$ and incorrectly selects the divisor. Since $42 \div 6 = 7$, the answer is positive $7$.
This multiplies $42$ by $6$ instead of dividing, and it also keeps a negative sign. The correct calculation is $42 \div 6 = 7$, with a positive result.

cards.front: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a [ ___ ] answer, but two negatives added give a [ ___ ] answer.
cards.back: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a positive answer, but two negatives added give a negative answer.

options.text: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a positive answer, but two negatives added give a negative answer.
options.explanation: Numbers with the same negative sign produce a positive result when multiplied or divided. Adding two negative numbers moves further below zero, so the sum is negative.

options.text: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a positive answer, but two negatives added give a positive answer.
options.explanation: The multiplication and division rule is applied correctly, but adding two negatives does not cancel their signs. Their magnitudes combine below zero, so the sum is negative.

options.text: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a negative answer, but two negatives added give a negative answer.
options.explanation: The addition rule is applied correctly, but two numbers with the same negative sign produce a positive result when multiplied or divided, not a negative result.

options.text: Two negatives multiplied or divided give a negative answer, but two negatives added give a positive answer.
options.explanation: This reverses both sign rules. Two negatives give a positive result when multiplied or divided, while adding two negatives combines their magnitudes to give a negative result.

cards.front: A number is multiplied by $6$ to give $-18$. What is the number?

options.explanation: Divide both sides of the equation by $6$. Since $-18 \div 6=-3$, multiplying the resulting number by $6$ gives the required $-18$.
Dropping the negative sign is the tempting error here. A positive number multiplied by $6$ remains positive, while $-18 \div 6=-3$.
Adding $6$ to $-18$ does not reverse multiplication by $6$. The inverse operation is division, and $-18 \div 6=-3$.
Multiplying $-18$ by $6$ repeats the original operation instead of undoing it. Dividing $-18$ by $6$ gives the correct number, $-3$.

cards.front: A number divided by $-4$ gives $5$. What is the number?

options.explanation: Undo division by $-4$ by multiplying $5$ by $-4$. A positive multiplied by a negative is negative, so the original number is $-20$.
Ignoring the negative divisor causes this sign error. The original number must be $5 \times -4=-20$, because $-20 \div -4=5$.
Dividing $5$ by $-4$ repeats division rather than reversing it. Division by $-4$ must be undone by multiplication, giving $5 \times -4=-20$.
Treating the divisor as something to add produces this result, but addition does not undo division. Multiplying $5$ by $-4$ gives the original number, $-20$.

cards.front: Continue the sequence: $13, 8, 3, \ldots$

options.explanation: Each term is $5$ less than the previous term: $13$ becomes $8$, then $3$, then $-2$, and finally $-7$.
The first continuation correctly subtracts $5$, but the next subtracts only $4$. The common difference remains $-5$, so the terms are $-2, -7$.
This loses one unit when crossing zero by treating $3-5$ as positive $2$. Subtracting $5$ consistently gives $3-5=-2$, followed by $-7$.
This subtracts $6$ from $3$ for the first missing term. The established step is subtracting $5$, so the next two terms are $-2, -7$.

cards.front: A temperature of $-5^\circ\text{C}$ rises by $8^\circ\text{C}$. What is the new temperature?

options.explanation: A rise means add $8$ to the starting temperature. Moving eight degrees upward from $-5^\circ\text{C}$ passes zero and reaches $3^\circ\text{C}$.
This treats the rise as a fall by subtracting $8$. A rise requires $-5+8$, which passes through zero and gives $3^\circ\text{C}$.
Adding the magnitudes ignores that the starting temperature is below zero. From $-5^\circ\text{C}$, five degrees reach zero and three more reach $3^\circ\text{C}$.
The magnitude $8-5=3$ is correct, but keeping the negative sign is not. The rise is greater than five degrees, so it passes zero and reaches $3^\circ\text{C}$.

cards.front: What is the difference between $-5^\circ\text{C}$ and $6^\circ\text{C}$?

options.explanation: The difference is the distance between the temperatures. It takes $5^\circ\text{C}$ to move from $-5^\circ\text{C}$ to zero and another $6^\circ\text{C}$ to reach $6^\circ\text{C}$, totalling $11^\circ\text{C}$.
Subtracting the magnitudes, $6-5$, ignores that the temperatures lie on opposite sides of zero. Their distance is $5+6=11^\circ\text{C}$.
Calculating $-5-6$ gives a directed change rather than the positive distance between the temperatures. The difference is the magnitude of the gap, $11^\circ\text{C}$.
This counts only the distance from $-5^\circ\text{C}$ to zero. The additional distance from zero to $6^\circ\text{C}$ makes the total difference $11^\circ\text{C}$.
